Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py
  tests/test_pipeline_queue.py

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md, sections "Queue management" and "Guest silence". Read it in the worktree before writing code. Where this brief and the spec differ, the spec wins and you say so in a comment.

WHY. The podcast must keep six episodes moving at all times, and the owner must be told when it thins out. Today nothing counts the pipeline. The named subtle failure is a queue count that LOOKS healthy while several episodes are actually stalled guests who went quiet, so the honesty of the count matters more than the count.

BUILD server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py — stdlib only, pure functions. It reads episode data dicts that a caller supplies; it does NOT walk the filesystem itself, so it stays testable.

  TARGET_IN_FLIGHT = 6     # owner's target; at or above this, no new outreach
  ESCALATE_BELOW = 3       # below this, alert AND increase outreach
  STALL_SILENCE_DAYS = 14  # owner: no response for 14 days is stalled

  is_stalled(episode, *, now) -> (bool, str)
      An episode is STALLED when EITHER holds (owner decision 2026-07-30):
        * it has no firm follow-up date on the calendar, or
        * there has been no response for STALL_SILENCE_DAYS.
      Either alone is sufficient. Return the reason string naming which fired.
      An episode that is already recorded (past the recording stage) is NOT
      stalled by guest silence, because the guest's job is done; say so in a
      comment and enforce it.

  in_flight(episodes, *, now) -> dict
      Counts episodes between candidate-approved and published, EXCLUDING
      stalled ones. Returns {"count": int, "counted": [ids], "stalled":
      [{"id","reason"}], "published": [ids], "not_started": [ids]}.
      A stalled episode must never appear in "counted".

  queue_status(episodes, *, now) -> dict
      Returns {"count", "target", "healthy": bool, "should_outreach": bool,
      "escalate": bool, "reason": str, "stalled": [...]}.
      Rules: healthy when count >= TARGET_IN_FLIGHT; should_outreach when
      count < TARGET_IN_FLIGHT; escalate when count < ESCALATE_BELOW.
      escalate implies should_outreach — the owner said alert AND refill, never
      alert and wait.

  Every threshold is a named module constant with a one-line rationale. Accept
  `now` as a parameter everywhere; never call datetime.now() inside a pure
  function, so tests are deterministic.

TESTS (tests/test_pipeline_queue.py; at least 6):
 (1) six healthy episodes: healthy True, should_outreach False, escalate False;
 (2) five healthy: should_outreach True, escalate False;
 (3) NEGATIVE and the most important: six episodes where three are stalled
     reports count 3, escalate True, and the three stalled ids listed. A stalled
     episode must NOT be counted — this is the named subtle failure;
 (4) NEGATIVE: an episode with no firm follow-up date is stalled even when it
     replied yesterday, because either condition alone suffices;
 (5) NEGATIVE: an episode silent 20 days but WITH a firm date is still stalled
     (silence alone suffices), while one silent 3 days WITH a date is not;
 (6) an already-recorded episode is not stalled by guest silence;
 (7) escalate always implies should_outreach;
 (8) determinism: same inputs and same `now` give identical output.
tasks.verified: honest in-flight count that excludes stalled guests, with escalate-and-refill below three

tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/candidate_vetting.py
  tests/test_candidate_vetting.py

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md, section "Candidate sourcing and vetting". Read it in the worktree first.

WHY. Guests arrive from four channels: referral from a past guest, outbound prospecting list, inbound application, and the owner's own network. Something must decide who is worth inviting without the owner in the loop.

THE RULE, and get this exactly right: there are four criteria and meeting ANY ONE of them qualifies a candidate. They are ALTERNATIVES, not a checklist. The owner said so explicitly on 2026-07-30: "any of those 4 are good not all four together just 1 out of 4 is fine". A system requiring all four would reject nearly everyone and starve the very queue this exists to fill. This is the single most important behaviour in the module.

BUILD server/pipeline/candidate_vetting.py — stdlib only, pure functions:

  CRITERIA = ("practice_leader_with_story", "has_audience_or_will_share",
              "fills_editorial_gap", "warm_connection_or_referrer")

  evaluate_candidate(candidate, *, recent_topics=()) -> dict
      Returns {"qualified": bool, "met": [criterion ids], "unknown":
      [criterion ids], "failed": [criterion ids], "reason": str}.
      qualified is True when len(met) >= MIN_CRITERIA_MET (named constant = 1,
      with a comment recording the owner decision and the date).
      A criterion that cannot be determined from the supplied candidate record
      is UNKNOWN, never met. Unknown must not qualify anyone: absence of
      evidence is not evidence.
      fills_editorial_gap is evaluated against `recent_topics` supplied by the
      caller; with no recent_topics supplied it is UNKNOWN, not met, because the
      module cannot know the slate on its own.

  rank_candidates(candidates, *, recent_topics=()) -> list
      Qualified candidates sorted by how many criteria they met (descending),
      then deterministically by a stable key so equal candidates never reorder
      between runs. Unqualified candidates are excluded, not sorted last.

  Do NOT invent scoring weights, thresholds, or extra criteria beyond the four.
  Do NOT call a model. Judgement beyond these four criteria is out of scope.

TESTS (tests/test_candidate_vetting.py; at least 6):
 (1) THE CORE RULE: a candidate meeting exactly ONE criterion is qualified;
 (2) a candidate meeting all four is qualified and outranks a one-criterion one;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a candidate meeting ZERO criteria is not qualified and the reason
     names that none were met;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a candidate whose only "met" criterion is actually UNKNOWN is not
     qualified — unknown never qualifies;
 (5) fills_editorial_gap is UNKNOWN when no recent_topics are supplied, and
     evaluated when they are;
 (6) NEGATIVE: rank_candidates excludes unqualified candidates entirely rather
     than ranking them last;
 (7) determinism: two candidates meeting the same number of criteria always sort
     in the same order across runs;
 (8) a referral-sourced candidate with a credible referrer qualifies on that
     criterion alone.
tasks.verified: any-one-of-four vetting so the queue fills, with unknown never qualifying a candidate

tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no real sending.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/send_safety.py
  tests/test_send_safety.py

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md, section "Compensating controls (required because the human gate is gone)". Read it in the worktree first.

WHY THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL. The owner removed the per-episode human approval for outbound sends on 2026-07-30 ("override it, risk is low here for now"). That decision removed the only human between an automated system and a real person's inbox. These controls are what carry the safety load in its absence. The spec states plainly that an implementation shipping without them has taken the override without the protection that justified it.

BUILD server/pipeline/send_safety.py — stdlib only, pure decision functions. It never sends anything; it decides whether a send may proceed.

  DAILY_SEND_CAP = 25          # halt-and-escalate ceiling, not a throttle
  KILL_SWITCH_ENV = "PODCAST_AUTO_KILL"

  verify_recipient(action, *, guest_record) -> (bool, str)
      The recipient address on the action must match the address on the guest
      record for that episode, compared case-insensitively with surrounding
      whitespace stripped. A mismatch, a missing address on either side, or more
      than one recipient returns False with a reason. Never "helpfully" correct
      an address; a mismatch ABORTS.

  within_send_cap(sent_today, *, cap=DAILY_SEND_CAP) -> (bool, str)
      False once sent_today >= cap. The reason must say the run halts and
      escalates rather than continuing, because a runaway loop is the failure
      this cap exists for.

  kill_switch_engaged(env=None) -> bool
      True when the kill-switch env var is set to any truthy value ("1", "true",
      "yes", case-insensitive). A malformed or unexpected value must be treated
      as ENGAGED, not ignored: a kill switch that fails open is not a kill
      switch. Document that choice in a comment.

  may_send(action, *, guest_record, sent_today, ledger_has_key, env=None) -> dict
      The single decision function. Returns {"allowed": bool, "reason": str,
      "checks": {name: bool}}. It allows a send only when ALL hold:
        * kill switch not engaged
        * an idempotency_key is present and non-empty on the action
        * ledger_has_key(idempotency_key) is False (never re-send a recorded key)
        * recipient verified against the guest record
        * within the daily cap
      Evaluate the kill switch FIRST and return immediately when engaged, so an
      emergency stop does not depend on any other check succeeding or on the
      loop being healthy.
      Any exception raised by ledger_has_key results in DENY with a reason, never
      allow: an unreadable ledger cannot be read as "not sent yet".

TESTS (tests/test_send_safety.py; at least 7):
 (1) a fully valid action is allowed and every check reports True;
 (2) NEGATIVE: kill switch engaged denies even when everything else is perfect,
     and denies FIRST (assert other checks were not required to pass);
 (3) NEGATIVE: a kill-switch value of "maybe" or "" is treated as ENGAGED —
     fail-closed;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a recipient that differs from the guest record denies, and the
     reason names the mismatch. Include a near-miss case differing only by case
     or trailing whitespace that SHOULD pass;
 (5) NEGATIVE: an action whose idempotency key is already in the ledger denies,
     proving a retry cannot duplicate a send;
 (6) NEGATIVE: a missing or empty idempotency key denies;
 (7) NEGATIVE: at the daily cap denies and the reason says halt-and-escalate;
 (8) NEGATIVE: a ledger lookup that raises denies rather than allowing.
tasks.verified: the compensating controls the autonomy override depends on: fail-closed kill switch, idempotency, recipient verification, daily cap
